title: Espresso Dial-In Drift by Bean Age
dataSources: Sourdough monitor (`sourdough:reading`), BBQ/sous-vide probes (`bbq:probe`), fridge/freezer/oven temperature (`kitchen:appliance`), espresso shots (`espresso:shot`), pantry inventory (`pantry:item`), kombucha brew (`kombucha:reading`).
app: ESP32/ESPHome kitchen sensors (sourdough rise, BBQ/sous-vide probes, fridge/freezer temperature), espresso-shot logs, and pantry inventory via MQTT and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot
| stats avg(shot_time_s) as avg_time, avg(yield_g) as avg_yield by bean_name bean_age_days

description: Shows how extraction behaviour shifts as beans age, helping you notice when the grind or dose drift is really a freshness drift.
value: Dial-in consistency is easier when freshness is part of the picture; this query links shot behaviour to bean age explicitly.
implementation: Forward espresso shot logs with bean age metadata; review older beans that are drifting outside your normal extraction window.
visualization: Scatter plot of bean age versus average shot time.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Kitchen, Cooking & Fermentation — typical feeds: Sourdough monitor (`sourdough:reading`), BBQ/sous-vide probes (`bbq:probe`), fridge/freezer/oven temperature (`kitchen:appliance`), espresso shots (`espresso:shot`), pantry inventory (`pantry:item`), .
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `espresso:shot`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=espresso:shot`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** ESP32/ESPHome kitchen sensors (sourdough rise, BBQ/sous-vide probes, fridge/freezer temperature), espresso-shot logs, and pantry inventory via MQTT and Splunk HEC..

**Author notes:** Forward espresso shot logs with bean age metadata; review older beans that are drifting outside your normal extraction window.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "espresso:shot", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Espresso Dial-In Drift by Bean Age** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=espresso:shot`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `bean_age_days` (> 21) after avg — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `avg_time`, `bean_age_days`, `bean_name`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot
| stats avg(shot_time_s) as avg_time, avg(yield_g) as avg_yield by bean_name bean_age_days
| where bean_age_days>21 AND (avg_time<22 OR avg_time>35)
| sort bean_age_days
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table avg_time, bean_age_days, bean_name
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `bean_age_days` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(bean_age_days) AS p50 perc90(bean_age_days) AS p90 perc99(bean_age_days) AS p99 max(bean_age_days) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.15.16: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Scatter Plot Of Bean Age Versus Average Shot Time (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `espresso:shot` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=espresso:shot | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
